question: The first electric tattoo machine was adapted from an office gadget for copying documents. Which famous inventor created that gadget?
source_excerpt: based on the rotary technology of Thomas Edison's autographic printing pen

extra.why_interesting: Players picture tattooing as an outlaw art invented in back rooms; it turns out the buzzing machine descends from an office gadget by the most famous inventor of all, and that name is a guess players can reach and feel clever about.
extra.verification_notes: O'Reilly's 1891 patented tattoo machine was adapted from Thomas Edison's electric pen duplicating device, per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_O%27Reilly

explanation: Edison's electric pen punched tiny holes in paper to make copying stencils. A New York tattooist realised the same buzzing needle could carry ink into skin and patented the idea in 1891.

question: Your body actually tries to remove a fresh tattoo. Special cells swallow the ink but can't digest it, so they just hold it in place for years. Which body system do those cells belong to?
topic: Tattoo studios: machines, ink and flash sheets
source_excerpt: the capture of ink by macrophages was associated with the induction of apoptosis in both human and murine models

extra.why_interesting: Players assume a tattoo lasts simply because ink is 'stuck' under the skin. In fact the body is actively trying to remove it. Cells that are meant to clear invaders swallow the pigment, can't break it down, and pass it to new cells when they die. The defence system ends up preserving the design. The stem's hint about cells that try to clean things up gives a clear path to reason it out.
extra.verification_notes: Tattoo ink is captured by macrophages (immune cells), so 'immune system' is correct; the 2025 PNAS study supports this and nothing newer overturns it (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41289395/).

explanation: The ink is held by macrophages, the immune system's clean-up cells. When one dies, a new one swallows the same pigment, so your defences keep your tattoo in place for life.
